ceiling_directive: Close the estimator-independent gap on the full frozen predictable class by proving either a uniform O(b_{nm}) estimator or a constant-order minimax converse.
improvement_directive: Resolve the b_{nm}-to-constant minimax gap for the same normalized maximum-row subspace loss: construct an observed-data estimator with uniformly shrinking risk, ideally O(b_{nm}), or strengthen the endogenous-target construction into an estimator-independent constant lower bound.
critique: The central theorem proves only c b_{nm} <= R^*_{nm} <= C(1 wedge a^{loose}_{nm}), and bounded outcomes make the stated upper endpoint constant in the principal fixed-complexity regime, leaving the minimax rate unresolved. The endogenous-target construction disproves b_{nm}-attainment only for recorded IPW–SVD and therefore supplies no converse explaining whether the constant upper endpoint is necessary. The blind diagnostic is controlled only at the nonshrinking d_{nm} resolution, while the simultaneous bands are conservative direct-IPW union-bound bands rather than a sharp inference result. The framing accurately discloses these limitations, but the delivered contribution remains a lower benchmark, a loose constant upper bound, and an estimator-specific failure example rather than the field-level frontier suggested by the title.
